title: Customer Churn Analysis Report – Key Findings
executive_summary: The analysis of 731 customers reveals an overall churn rate of 37.2% with modest variation across subscription plans and signup cohorts. Monthly contract holders churn at more than double the rate of annual contract holders, highlighting contract length as a key driver. An at‑risk segment of 100 customers shows a high churn of 71%. Tenure averages 21 months and satisfaction averages 3.42 on a 5‑point scale, though 27 scores are missing. Lifetime value (LTV) differs sharply by plan, with Premium customers delivering roughly $1,839 versus $466 for Basic, a 295% increase. These insights point to opportunities for targeted retention, contract restructuring, and plan‑specific value enhancement.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 731 customers, with an overall churn rate of 37.2% and an average monthly fee of $42.14.
Churn rates differ by subscription plan, with Basic customers experiencing the highest churn (38.6%), followed by Standard (36.5%) and Premium (35.3%).
Churn by signup cohort shows a slight variation across years, highest for the 2024 cohort (38.1%) and lowest for the 2023 cohort (36.4%).
Customers on Monthly contracts churn at a rate 119% higher than those on Annual contracts, indicating a substantial increase.
The identified at‑risk segment comprises 100 customers, of whom 71% have churned.
Across all customers, average tenure is 21 months (median 19, std dev 13.3). The mean satisfaction score is 3.42, with 27 customers missing a score.
Lifetime value varies strongly by plan: Premium customers generate $1,839, Standard $878, and Basic $466. Premium LTV is 295% higher than Basic.

limitations: The cleaning stage failed, so residual data quality issues (e.g., duplicate rows, inconsistent formats) may remain.
Missing values for satisfaction_score (27 customers) were excluded from mean calculations, potentially biasing the satisfaction estimate.
The analysis relies on simple aggregations; causal relationships (e.g., why contract type affects churn) are not established.
At‑risk segment definition uses arbitrary thresholds (≥5 support tickets, ≤2 satisfaction) and may miss other at‑risk customers.
conclusion: Churn is substantial overall and especially high among monthly contract holders, suggesting that encouraging longer‑term contracts could improve retention. Plan‑specific strategies are warranted: Basic plans show the highest churn, while Premium plans deliver the greatest revenue per customer. Targeted outreach to the identified at‑risk segment could mitigate its 71% churn rate. Improving data cleaning processes will enhance future analyses.
